text:
sarah (CEO): quick follow-up from today's all-hands — a few asked for clarity on the reorg rollout and how hiring headcount is being allocated. I'll lay out the timeline and priorities here, ask follow-ups below.
jen (Recruiting): thanks! will this include a hiring freeze or just reprioritization?
dave (CTO): no company-wide freeze. we're shifting open req prioritization toward infra/runtime, Dedicated capacity, and customer-facing product teams for the next two quarters.
lisa (Dir Eng): to be concrete — teams working on latency, autoscaling, and model-serving reliability get top priority for req approvals.
mike (Product): how should PMs request priority for a role? is there a form or will managers coordinate with recruiters?
maria (People Ops): managers should open a prioritization ticket in the hiring queue (link: internal/hires) and tag @jen + @lisa. we'll triage weekly.
raj (Eng): are we still approving lateral IC hires or mostly seniors and staff-level for the infra push?
dave (CTO): mix — we want a pyramid: ~60% senior+ (to move projects fast), ~40% mid-level for capacity. junior hires will be considered where we have strong mentorship lanes.
sarah (CEO): timeline: reorg org charts finalized by end of week, role mapping/backfills over next 3 weeks, new reqs prioritized immediately and hiring intensity ramping in Q2.
jen (Recruiting): for candidates in pipeline — we will continue interviews. if a role is deprioritized we'll notify candidates and reopen when it becomes a priority.
maria (People Ops): internal mobility — if you're interested in moving into a prioritized team, ping your manager + post in #internal-moves. we'll fast-track internal transfers.
mike (Product): any impact on hiring for growth/expansion projects (PLG tooling, UX)?
sarah (CEO): growth/product roles are still funded but will compete for headcount — expect slower cadence; critical customer projects keep priority.
lisa (Dir Eng): org structure: two infra pods will merge operationally into "Serving" and "Platform" — managers will keep the same IC leads for now; some TLs may be reassigned. we'll share a visual org map by Friday.
raj (Eng): will there be manager changes or new manager hires?
dave (CTO): a few new manager slots are approved (mainly for Dedicated and Private ops). we are avoiding unnecessary manager hires elsewhere.
jen (Recruiting): quick ask — hiring managers: please update JD + leveling rubric before posting. we had a few mismatches last month.
sarah (CEO): compensation/banding — no immediate band resets. any role-level exceptions will be handled by People Ops on a case-by-case basis.
maria (People Ops): for relocation/visa: existing offers remain valid; new reqs that require sponsorship will be evaluated case-by-case due to regional budget differences.
raj (Eng): will we still interview for research/applied ML roles?
dave (CTO): yes — but on a smaller quota. priority for ML hires will be roles that directly improve inference efficiency or model serving.
mike (Product): is there a place to see the exact headcount allocation?
maria (People Ops): we'll publish a simple headcount spreadsheet (read-only) with buckets: Serving/Runtime, Dedicated/Infra, Product/Growth, Research/ML, Customer Excellence by EOD Wednesday.
jen (Recruiting): note: if you have an urgent hire tied to a customer SLA, mark the ticket "urgent-sla" and include the customer name. that moves you to the top of the weekly triage.
lisa (Dir Eng): happy to take 1:1s with managers who have complicated team questions — DM me and I'll schedule a sync.
sarah (CEO): thanks everyone. we'll keep this thread updated with the org map + headcount doc. if folks want an AMA, we can host a short follow-up asap. :thumbsup: 
raj (Eng): thanks — appreciate the clarity.
jen (Recruiting): adding note: updating interview loops this week to match new priorities; expect some panel changes.
oncall-bot: reminder — all-hands follow-up doc uploaded: internal/allhands/2026-03-19-notes.md
